B1:
Touched fires many times: once per character part that touches (feet, legs, HumanoidRootPart) and again on each contact, all in the same frame before Destroy takes effect, so 3-5 handlers each add 10. Destroy doesn't stop events already queued (and with deferred signals they all run). Also hit.Parent may be an accessory (no player), fine here.
Fix: debounce with a consumed flag set before awarding, server-side:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local part = script.Parent
local taken = false
part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
	if taken then return end
	local char = hit:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
	local plr = char and Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(char)
	if not plr then return end
	local hum = char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
	taken = true -- set before any yield/award
	local coins = plr:FindFirstChild("leaderstats") and plr.leaderstats:FindFirstChild("Coins")
	if coins then coins.Value += 10 end
	part:Destroy()
end)
```
For respawning coins, use a per-player debounce table or disable CanTouch, and keep the authoritative balance in server data.
B2:
With StreamingEnabled the client only has instances near the player (within the streaming radius); far-away doors (and possibly the Hotel model's parts) haven't streamed in, so direct indexing at script start errors. Parts can also stream out later.
Fix 1: WaitForChild along the path (with timeout handling), and handle streaming out:
```lua
local hotel = workspace:WaitForChild("Map"):WaitForChild("Buildings"):WaitForChild("Hotel")
local door = hotel:WaitForChild("Door", 30)
if door then door.Touched:Connect(onTouch) end
```
(but it may still stream out later, and WaitForChild may wait forever.)
Fix 2 (better): tag doors with CollectionService ("Door") and use GetInstanceAddedSignal/GetTagged + InstanceRemovedSignal to connect/disconnect as they stream in and out. Alternatives: make the Hotel/door Model ModelStreamingMode = Atomic or Persistent (Persistent always present on client, costs memory), or handle door touches on the server (server always has everything) and replicate the result. For a teleport destination use player:RequestStreamAroundAsync.
B3:
Bugs:
1. Always returns PurchaseGranted, even if pcall failed (charged, nothing saved) - must return NotProcessedYet on failure so Roblox retries.
2. No idempotency: no PurchaseId check, so retries/duplicate callbacks grant twice (double coins).
3. GetAsync + SetAsync is a race (read-modify-write across servers, and it overwrites concurrent session saves); use UpdateAsync atomically.
4. plr may be nil if the player left: plr.UserId errors inside pcall -> still Granted. Use info.PlayerId, and if the player isn't in the server return NotProcessedYet (or grant to stored data idempotently).
5. Ignores info.ProductId (every product gives 100), and writes a separate store that may conflict with the session/profile data (the profile's later save overwrites it -> lost coins).
Corrected behaviour: look up handler by ProductId; check player present; in one UpdateAsync on the player's data, if PurchaseId already in a receipts list, keep; else add coins and record PurchaseId (cap list size); return PurchaseGranted only if that succeeded; on any error/nil player/unknown product return NotProcessedYet. Update the live session/leaderstats after the commit. Only one script sets ProcessReceipt.
B4:
Remote arguments are serialized: tables are copied as plain data, metatables are stripped, and functions can't be sent. So the client gets {Name="Rifle", Ammo=30} without the Weapon metatable -> w:Fire is nil. (Also mixed/non-string keys get dropped/converted.)
Instances are sent as references; if the client can't see the instance (ServerStorage never replicates to clients), the reference arrives as nil.
Fix: send plain data and reconstruct on the client: `remote:FireClient(plr, {Name=w.Name, Ammo=w.Ammo})`, then client `local w = setmetatable(data, Weapon)` using a shared Weapon module in ReplicatedStorage (behaviour lives in shared code, not in the message). For the part: put it in ReplicatedStorage (or clone it into workspace / a replicated container) before firing, or send an identifier (name/asset key) and let the client find/clone its own copy. Ensure it has replicated before the client uses it (the instance must exist on the client when the event is processed).
B5:
workspace:Raycast's second argument is the direction vector and its LENGTH is the ray length. `.Unit` makes it 1 stud long, so it only hits things within 1 stud of origin. (Also the ray may start inside the shooter's own character/gun and hit that, and no RaycastParams are used.)
Fix:
```lua
local MAX_RANGE = 500
local dir = (target - origin).Unit * MAX_RANGE -- or (target - origin) for exactly to target
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = { shooterCharacter }
local r = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
if r then print(r.Instance, r.Position) end
```
Guard against target == origin (Unit of zero vector is NaN). Do the authoritative raycast on the server with validated origin.
B6:
When the last player leaves, the server shuts down; PlayerRemoving fires, but the server may close before the async SetAsync completes (the yielding save is cut off), and on shutdown (update/close) PlayerRemoving may not finish at all. game:BindToClose is the hook that keeps the server alive (up to ~30 seconds) while saves finish.
Fix:
- Save from a shared save(player) function used by PlayerRemoving, autosave (every 1-5 min) and BindToClose.
- In BindToClose, save every remaining player in parallel (task.spawn) and wait until all done (or ~25s), skipping players already saved/being saved (dedupe with a saving flag).
- In Studio, BindToClose saves can be skipped (RunService:IsStudio()) to avoid hangs.
- Use UpdateAsync with session locking rather than SetAsync, pcall + retries.
```lua
game:BindToClose(function()
  local pending = 0
  for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do pending += 1
    task.spawn(function() save(p, true); pending -= 1 end) end
  local t = os.clock()
  while pending > 0 and os.clock() - t < 25 do task.wait() end
end)
```
B7:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local remote = game.ReplicatedStorage.Remotes.UseAbility
local COOLDOWN = 2
local lastUse: {[Player]: number} = {}

remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, abilityId)
	if typeof(abilityId) ~= "string" or #abilityId > 32 then return end
	local now = os.clock()
	local last = lastUse[player]
	if last and now - last < COOLDOWN then return end -- spam ignored silently
	lastUse[player] = now -- set before any yield
	local char = player.Character
	local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
	performAbility(player, abilityId) -- server-validated effect
end)

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	lastUse[player] = nil -- no leak
end)
```
Server owns the clock (client cooldown is only for UI). For per-ability cooldowns key by player then ability, and clear the whole player entry on leave.
B8:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local MPS = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
local DSS = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local store = DSS:GetDataStore("PlayerData_v1")
local GEMS100 = 123456
local handlers = { [GEMS100] = function(data) data.Gems = (data.Gems or 0) + 100 end }

MPS.ProcessReceipt = function(info) -- the ONLY assignment in the game
	local handler = handlers[info.ProductId]
	if not handler then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
	local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(info.PlayerId)
	if not player then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end -- retried on rejoin
	local granted = false
	local ok, err = pcall(function()
		store:UpdateAsync("u_" .. info.PlayerId, function(data)
			data = data or { Gems = 0, Receipts = {} }
			data.Receipts = data.Receipts or {}
			if data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] then granted = true; return nil end -- already granted
			handler(data)
			data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] = os.time() -- prune old entries in practice
			granted = true
			return data
		end)
	end)
	if not ok then warn("receipt failed", err); return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
	if granted then
		-- refresh live session / leaderstats from saved value here (no re-grant)
		return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
	end
	return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet
end
```
Note: transform has no side effects besides the data (granted flag reset is safe since retries recompute). If you use a session-locked profile, apply the grant + PurchaseId to the profile and save it in the same commit instead of a separate write, otherwise the profile save overwrites it.
B9:
```lua
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local menu = script.Parent:WaitForChild("Menu") -- Frame
local info = TweenInfo.new(0.4, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)
local OPEN = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5, 0)
local CLOSED = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1.5, 0)
menu.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
local current: Tween?

local function open()
	if current then current:Cancel() end
	menu.Position = CLOSED
	menu.Visible = true
	current = TweenService:Create(menu, info, { Position = OPEN })
	current:Play()
end

local function close()
	if current then current:Cancel() end
	local t = TweenService:Create(menu, info, { Position = CLOSED })
	current = t
	t.Completed:Connect(function(state)
		if state == Enum.PlaybackState.Completed and current == t then
			menu.Visible = false
		end
	end)
	t:Play()
end
```
The Completed check stops a close interrupted by a re-open from hiding the menu. (Could use Quad In for the close for feel.)
B10:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local MAX_RANGE = 200
local DAMAGE = 20

local function shoot(player: Player, targetPos: Vector3)
	if typeof(targetPos) ~= "Vector3" or targetPos ~= targetPos then return end -- type + NaN
	local char = player.Character
	local head = char and char:FindFirstChild("Head")
	local myHum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if not head or not myHum or myHum.Health <= 0 then return end
	local origin = head.Position
	local offset = targetPos - origin
	if offset.Magnitude < 1e-3 then return end
	local dir = offset.Unit * MAX_RANGE
	local params = RaycastParams.new()
	params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
	params.FilterDescendantsInstances = { char }
	local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
	if not result then return end
	local model = result.Instance:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
	local hum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if hum and hum.Health > 0 then
		hum:TakeDamage(DAMAGE) -- respects ForceField
	end
	return result
end
```
Call from a validated, rate-limited remote; the server computes origin from the server-side head, never trusting a client origin.
B11:
```lua
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local TAG = "KillBrick"
local connections: {[Instance]: RBXScriptConnection} = {}

local function onAdded(inst: Instance)
	if not inst:IsA("BasePart") or connections[inst] then return end
	connections[inst] = inst.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
		local model = hit:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
		local hum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
		if hum and hum.Health > 0 then
			hum.Health = 0
		end
	end)
end

local function onRemoved(inst: Instance)
	local c = connections[inst]
	if c then c:Disconnect(); connections[inst] = nil end
end

CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(TAG):Connect(onAdded)
CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(TAG):Connect(onRemoved)
for _, inst in CollectionService:GetTagged(TAG) do onAdded(inst) end
```
Connect the signals before iterating GetTagged so nothing is missed; InstanceRemoved also fires when a tagged part is destroyed, so connections are cleaned up.

```lua
local TeleportService = game:GetService("TeleportService")
local MAX_ATTEMPTS, RETRY_DELAY = 3, 2

local function safeTeleport(placeId: number, players: {Player}, teleportData: any?)
	local options = Instance.new("TeleportOptions")
	if teleportData ~= nil then options:SetTeleportData(teleportData) end
	for attempt = 1, MAX_ATTEMPTS do

```

B13:
(a) Buy: client -> server RemoteEvent (or RemoteFunction InvokeServer if the client wants an immediate success/fail reply). Client sends only intent (itemId). The server validates: item exists, price from server catalog, balance check, rate limit, ownership; deducts and grants; balance lives in server-side player data (saved in DataStore), never on the client.
(b) Counter update: server -> client via a RemoteEvent FireClient (or just a replicated value: leaderstats IntValue / player attribute "Coins" that the client UI listens to with GetAttributeChangedSignal/.Changed). The client UI is display-only.
Why not RemoteFunction:InvokeClient for the UI: the server thread yields waiting on the client; an exploiter (or a client that disconnects or errors) can never return, hanging the server thread forever, or error, or return garbage; it has no timeout. The server doesn't need an answer to a UI refresh anyway, so a one-way RemoteEvent/replicated attribute is correct. Roblox docs warn against InvokeClient for this reason.
B14:
Teleport data (TeleportOptions:SetTeleportData / GetJoinData().TeleportData) is sent through the client: it can be read and tampered with by exploiters, has size limits, and is lost if the teleport fails or the player rejoins directly. Fine only for non-authoritative, cosmetic info (e.g. chosen loadout preferences you re-validate, a match id, party info).
DataStores: authoritative, persistent, but have budgets and eventual delays; with session locking you must save+release before teleport and the destination waits for the lock. MemoryStore (SortedMap/HashMap): fast, cross-server, expiring (TTL), good for transient handoff like the match assignment/loadout keyed by userId, with quota limits; not persistent.
Choice: coin balance stays in the DataStore (session-locked profile): save on leave from lobby, load in match place (the profile already contains it - no need to carry it). Loadout: either also in saved data, or write it to a MemoryStore HashMap keyed by userId (short TTL) before teleport and read it on arrival; teleport data at most carries non-trusted hints (match/server id) which the server validates. Never trust coins from teleport data.
B15:
Per-instance Scripts: 610 copies of the same code, each its own thread and connections; memory and script-scheduler overhead, slow to update (fix one bug in 400 places, copies drift), hard to tune centrally, scripts copied with packages, and they don't handle streaming well (on the client they may run before/after parts stream).
Tag-driven: tag instances with CollectionService ("Door", "Pickup", "Turret") in Studio or at spawn. One server Script (or a module per system loaded by a single bootstrap) per tag: a component/system module that, for each tagged instance, constructs an object (state, connections) and stores it in a map. Use GetTagged for existing ones plus GetInstanceAddedSignal for newly spawned/cloned/streamed-in ones and GetInstanceRemovedSignal (fires on Destroy or streaming out) to clean up connections (a Janitor/Trove per instance). Config via attributes on the instance. Shared logic lives once; client-side visuals (door animation, pickup bob) in a client system with the same pattern, which naturally handles StreamingEnabled since tags fire as instances stream in/out. Batch work: e.g. turrets updated in one Heartbeat loop over a list rather than 60 loops; spread updates, sleep far-away ones. Libraries: plain CollectionService, or component libraries (e.g. Component from RbxUtil).
B16:
Ownership: give the driver's client network ownership of the car's assembly (SetNetworkOwner(driver) on the VehicleSeat occupant change, or rely on auto ownership which gives the seated player ownership; set back to nil/server when they leave). Driving needs responsive, lag-free physics; server ownership would add round-trip latency to steering.
Risk: the owning client simulates the physics and the server accepts it, so an exploiter can teleport/fly the car, set any speed, ignore collisions, push other players' cars (ownership extends to connected assemblies), finish races instantly.
Server must validate: speed/acceleration caps vs car stats, position deltas per tick (no teleports, flying, going through walls - raycast between samples), checkpoints passed in order with plausible split times, lap/finish times above a minimum, the car's ownership only while seated (reclaim on exit), and anything rewarding (wins, currency) decided server-side. On violation: reset car to last valid checkpoint, take ownership back, or flag. (Server Authority mode is the 2026 alternative to get server-authoritative physics with prediction.)
B17:
Use an UnreliableRemoteEvent for aim/position streams and lower the rate (10-20 Hz, and only send on meaningful change).
Constraints (Roblox docs): best-effort, may be dropped, not ordered (later messages can arrive first), payload over 1,000 bytes is dropped, excess over the throttle (~500 requests/s per client shared per remote type) is dropped, not queued; messages with no connected handler are discarded.
Handling: send a sequence number or server timestamp and ignore older-than-latest packets on receipt; send absolute state (latest aim/position), never deltas, so a lost packet doesn't matter; keep payloads tiny (quantize floats, pack into a buffer, e.g. aim as two angles in int16, position via int32/fixed point); interpolate on observers; validate on server (rate limit, clamp values, NaN checks, position plausibility). Keep reliable RemoteEvents for things that must arrive (shots fired, hits, ability use). Character position already replicates via physics, so often you don't need to send it at all - send only aim direction.
B18:
Parallel Luau: put the NPC AI scripts under Actor instances (e.g. one Actor per group of ~10-25 NPCs, or a handful of Actors with work split), each Script inside does `task.desynchronize()` (or ConnectParallel on Heartbeat) to run raycasts (workspace:Raycast is parallel-safe), spatial queries and path scoring in parallel, then `task.synchronize()` to apply results (move humanoids, set properties, fire remotes). Alternatively use SharedTable or actor messaging (Actor:SendMessage/BindToMessageParallel) to distribute NPC ids.
Limitations: in the parallel phase you can only read the DataModel and call thread-safe APIs; writing most properties, creating/destroying instances, firing remotes, and many yielding APIs (PathfindingService:ComputeAsync is not parallel-safe) are errors and must be done in serial phase. Actors' scripts don't share Luau state (separate VMs): communicate via messages, attributes, SharedTable; require'd modules are per-actor copies. Each sync/desync has overhead, so batch work per actor rather than one actor per tiny task. Results apply one frame later effectively. Also reduce work: don't think every Heartbeat - stagger NPC updates (e.g. 5-10 Hz), skip NPCs far from players, cache paths.
B19:
Turn on Workspace.StreamingEnabled. Sensible settings: StreamingTargetRadius ~ 1024 default (lower, e.g. 512-768, for mobile-heavy dense maps), StreamingMinRadius ~ 64-128 (default 64) - must cover what gameplay needs immediately around the player; StreamOutBehavior = Opportunistic (streams out distant content to save memory; LowMemory streams out only under pressure); StreamingIntegrityMode = MinimumRadiusPause (or PauseOutsideLoadedArea) to stop players walking into unloaded areas. ModelStreamingMode per model: Atomic for models that must arrive whole (doors, vehicles, NPCs), Persistent only for few things that must always exist on the client (costs memory), PersistentPerPlayer for player-specific; enable Model LoD (ModelLevelOfDetail = StreamingMesh) for far imposters of big buildings.
Scripts: client code must not assume instances exist: use WaitForChild (with timeouts) or better CollectionService tags with InstanceAdded/Removed signals, handle streaming out (connections cleaned up, nil checks), use player:RequestStreamAroundAsync before teleporting/moving players or the camera to distant points, keep server logic server-side (server has everything). Move client-only references away from long direct paths like workspace.Map.X.Y. Test with Studio's streaming and low-memory device emulation.
B20:
Cause: 80 players x every 5 s = 960 writes/min, far above the write budget (per-server legacy 60 + 10 x players per minute, and per key writes should be several seconds apart; experience budget 300 + 20 x CCU). Excess requests queue; when the queue fills further requests are dropped (error 302 / "DataStore request was added to queue" warnings then failures), so saves are lost, and SetAsync also overwrites without conflict protection.
Better design: keep data in memory per session; autosave each player every 60-300 s (staggered so players don't all save at once), only if dirty; save on PlayerRemoving and BindToClose; use UpdateAsync with session locking (or ProfileStore); pcall with exponential backoff retries; check DataStoreService:GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before non-critical saves; one key per player (not many keys per player); save important events (purchases) immediately but via the same profile commit. Throttle combined writes so leaves and purchases always have budget.

B22:
Three core instances: InputContext (a group of actions you enable/disable and prioritise; Enabled, Priority, Sink), InputAction (the abstract action, with Type Bool, Direction1D/2D/3D or ViewportPosition), and InputBinding (maps a physical input to the action: KeyCode, PrimaryModifier/SecondaryModifier for chords, UIButton for touch buttons, Scale, axes for composite directions). Hierarchy: InputContext > InputAction > InputBinding(s); give each action keyboard/mouse, gamepad and touch bindings. IAS instances exist on client and server (CAS is client-only).
Signalling: a Bool action fires Pressed and Released, StateChanged(newState), and you can poll action:GetState() (true while held; vectors for direction types).
Precedence: give the menu's InputContext a higher Priority than the gameplay/default player-script contexts and set Sink = true so inputs bound in the menu context aren't passed to lower-priority contexts (e.g. ButtonA confirms instead of jumping); enable it when the menu opens and disable it on close. With Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem enabled the default controls are themselves IAS contexts, so this sinking applies to movement/jump.
B23:
Roblox's UI Styling system applies CSS-like rules to GuiObjects. Instances: StyleSheet (holds rules and tokens), StyleRule (a Selector like "TextButton", ".Primary" class via the instance's Tags, "#Name", descendant/child combinators, pseudo-states like ":hover"/":press", with property values set via SetProperty/SetProperties and a Priority), StyleLink (placed in a ScreenGui/LayerCollector, its StyleSheet property points at the sheet - this is how styles reach the UI tree; only one StyleSheet applies per tree), and StyleDerive (lets a sheet inherit from another sheet, e.g. a theme deriving from a base). Rules can nest (child StyleRules).
Tokens: define design tokens as attributes on the StyleSheet (e.g. sheet:SetAttribute("PrimaryColor", Color3...)) and reference them in rule values as "$PrimaryColor"; change the token once (or swap a derived theme sheet) and every rule using it updates. Rules apply to all matching instances; Priority resolves conflicts. StyleQuery (media/container queries) and Styling Transitions were still Studio betas as of Oct 2026.
B24:
Method: chat requires a completed age check, normally Facial Age Estimation via the camera (processed by a vendor, images deleted), with ID verification (13+) or parental controls able to correct it. Tested from December 2025 in Australia, New Zealand and the Netherlands; required worldwide from January 2026.
Age groups: under 9, 9-12, 13-15, 16-17, 18-20, 21+.
Restriction: users can chat only with their own group and the adjacent groups (one above and below), designed to stop under-16s chatting with adults; under-9s need parental consent for chat; Roblox Kids (5-8) have communication off by default; Trusted Connections let age-checked 13+ users chat more freely with people they know. Users who haven't checked can't chat. Messages simply don't appear to disallowed players. Devs can't read ages: use TextChatService:GetChatGroupsAsync, CanUsersChatAsync / CanUsersDirectChatAsync before private channels, and don't make gameplay depend on chat. (Policy and Age Rules 2026; Age Checks and Safety Features.)
